title: A Summit for the Landfall
premise: Edmund Montrose, a disgraced railroad engineer fleeing debts in the colonial port city of Vellamoor, accepts a dying prospector's map to the source of the Sarn River — a route through closed mountain lines that no survey has ever returned from. Pursued by the prospector's killers and shadowed by a company man who wants the source dammed for profit, Edmund joins forces with a runaway tea-estate girl and an exiled boatman who knows the river's moods. As the monsoon builds behind them, they discover the 'source' is a living glacial lake the company intends to destroy — and that Edmund's own compass once belonged to the surveyor who died protecting it. In the end, Edmund chooses to flood his own escape route, breaching the company's works so the river runs free, and the three survivors descend together as the first storm makes landfall.
about_author: Tamsin Galloway is the pen name of a former hydrographic surveyor who spent six years charting monsoon rivers before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people caught between maps and the terrain that refuses to obey them.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund Montrose, drowning in debt in the port city of Vellamoor, is summoned to a flophouse where a fevered prospector trades him a hand-drawn map of the Sarn's forbidden headwaters for a promise: carry it upstream or burn it. Within hours, men come asking questions, and Edmund flees with the map sewn into his coat. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance — a coward handed a duty he never asked for.

chapters.title: Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Edmund uses his old railroad credentials to slip past a checkpoint on a decommissioned mountain line, where he meets Asha, a runaway tea-estate girl hiding in a maintenance shed, and Karun, an exiled boatman who agrees to take them upriver. The prospector's killers ambush them at a trestle bridge; they escape by derailing a handcar, but the company man Rook now knows exactly who carries the map. POV: Edmund, with Asha's interlude. Emotional beat: strangers becoming accomplices.

chapters.title: Where the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: The ascent through gorges and abandoned survey camps reveals the truth: the 'source' is a living glacial lake, and Rook's company plans to dam and drain it, drowning the valley villages below. Edmund finds his own compass inscribed with the name of the surveyor who died defending the lake — his estranged father. Rook captures Asha as leverage, demanding the map. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the price of survival made personal; grief weaponized.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: In the storm's first hours, Edmund trades the map for Asha's freedom, then turns Rook's own blasting charges against the half-built dam works, releasing the lake's overflow down the natural channel and destroying the company's claim forever. Karun pilots them down the swollen river through the landfall itself, nearly losing everything. They reach the delta as the sky clears — broke, hunted, and unbroken, a family made by water. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: costly triumph; survival that finally means something.
